priorStories.headline: CBO estimates Iran operations cost $38 billion
priorStories.body:
The Congressional Budget Office estimated that Defense Department combat operations against Iran cost about $38 billion through August 1 and could add roughly $3 billion a month, depending on the conflict’s intensity.

CBO projected a 0.5% inflation increase in the first quarter of 2027 and said depleted munitions could take five years to replenish. The Pentagon disputed the finding that its stocks were insufficient.

priorStories.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 7,258 confirmed cases
priorStories.body:
Government figures listed 7,258 confirmed Ebola cases and 3,510 deaths across seven provinces in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, United Nations officials said.

Containment efforts were making progress in some places, but the epidemic was still growing elsewhere. A World Health Organization official said it was too early to conclude that the outbreak had peaked.

priorStories.headline: Hospital failures left infants unprotected from Letby
priorStories.body:
A British public inquiry found that failures by senior staff and dysfunctional management at the Countess of Chester Hospital allowed nurse Lucy Letby to harm infants. It concluded that earlier action could have prevented at least two murders.

The report recommended stronger neonatal safeguards, including protocols for suspected deliberate harm and consideration of cameras in cots and incubators. It did not examine Letby’s guilt or innocence.

priorStories.headline: Belarus justice system coordinated repression, UN finds
priorStories.body:
Independent United Nations experts found that Belarusian courts, police, security services, prosecutors and prison authorities acted in coordination to suppress government critics throughout the justice process.

The panel documented arbitrary arrests, torture, denial of legal safeguards, closed trials and harassment after release. Belarus, which has previously rejected UN criticism, did not immediately respond to the new findings.

candidates.summary: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte appeared at the International Criminal Court in The Hague for a hearing on his health and ability to stand trial. It was his first public appearance since his transfer to the court 18 months earlier. His lawyers argue that cognitive decline leaves him unfit for a trial scheduled to begin in November; Duterte did not speak during the hearing.
candidates.title: Duterte appears at ICC fitness hearing

candidates.summary: A structurally damaged residential building housing displaced families collapsed overnight in Gaza City. The Associated Press reported that 19 people were killed and 25 injured, with rescuers searching for others beneath the rubble. Earlier counts from Gaza civil defense cited by Reuters listed at least 12 deaths, including five children, and 14 injuries, illustrating that the toll was still developing.
candidates.title: Gaza building collapse kills at least 19

candidates.summary: Russian drones struck civilian transportation in southern Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said. Police reported that an attack on a passenger bus near Nikopol killed four men and a woman and injured seven people. A passenger train in the Mykolaiv region was also attacked repeatedly; officials said all 168 passengers and crew members were evacuated without injuries. Russia did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Russian drones strike Ukrainian bus and train

candidates.summary: India summoned Pakistan’s senior diplomat in New Delhi and instructed its representative in Islamabad to lodge protests over a collision between Pakistani and Indian naval vessels in the northern Arabian Sea. India said a Pakistani ship approached an Indian warship at high speed in international waters on Tuesday, violating a bilateral separation agreement. No major damage was reported, and Pakistan did not immediately respond.
candidates.title: India protests naval collision with Pakistan

candidates.summary: A Russian court convicted Russian-Canadian national Nikolai Zyuzev of high treason and sentenced him to seven years in a penal colony, according to the state news agency RIA. Russia’s Federal Security Service alleged that he trained leaders of ethnic-minority separatist movements abroad and distributed materials it classified as extremist. The report did not state how Zyuzev pleaded.
candidates.title: Russian court sentences dual national for treason

candidates.summary: Later reports raised the death toll from the overnight collapse of a war-damaged residential building sheltering displaced families in Gaza City. Reuters reported 20 deaths, while an Associated Press regional roundup reported at least 21. Rescue workers continued searching the wreckage.
candidates.title: Gaza building-collapse toll rises to at least 20

candidates.summary: The EU-backed Kosovo Specialist Chambers convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of war crimes and sentenced him to 25 years in prison. The court found him guilty of crimes including murder, torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary or illegal detention committed during the 1998-99 conflict. Thaci denied the charges, and both sides may appeal.
candidates.title: Kosovo tribunal sentences Thaci to 25 years

candidates.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen used her annual address to propose making Canada the EU’s first associate member, banning children under 13 from social media while creating restricted accounts for older minors, and establishing an EU mechanism for coordinated responses to drone incidents, sabotage and cyberattacks. The initiatives remain proposals requiring further development or approval.
candidates.title: EU chief outlines Canada, social-media and security proposals

candidates.summary: Belarus released 25 prisoners in exchange for further easing of U.S. sanctions, according to Reuters. The group included journalist Andrei Alyaksandrau and three musicians whose songs had been designated extremist materials. The United States lifted sanctions on two Belarusian companies, while the Viasna rights group said Belarus still held 886 political prisoners.
candidates.title: Belarus frees 25 prisoners in U.S. sanctions deal

candidates.summary: Syria’s parliament voted to abolish the Assad-era Counter-Terrorism Court and nullify the legal effects of its rulings, state television reported. The court, established in 2012, prosecuted thousands of Syrians and had been criticized by United Nations bodies over inadequate judicial safeguards and links to arbitrary detention and torture. The vote formalized steps already taken by Syria’s post-Assad authorities.
candidates.title: Syria votes to nullify Assad-era terrorism-court rulings

candidates.summary: France’s national health agency estimated that the country recorded at least 817 excess deaths during exceptionally hot weather from July 27 through August 20. The estimate, based on death certificates and including deaths from all causes, brought recorded excess mortality since June and the beginning of successive heatwaves to nearly 8,000. People aged 75 and older accounted for most of the excess deaths.
candidates.title: France reports 817 excess deaths during latest heatwaves

candidates.summary: Sweden summoned Iran’s ambassador and ordered an official at the Iranian Embassy in Stockholm to leave the country. The Swedish Foreign Ministry cited activity incompatible with the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations but did not specify what the official was accused of doing.
candidates.title: Sweden orders Iranian Embassy official to leave

candidates.summary: Ukraine presented parliament with a draft 2027 budget proposing record defense spending of 4.89 trillion hryvnias, about $110 billion and 12% above the current year. Defense would account for roughly two-thirds of the proposal’s total spending of 7.27 trillion hryvnias. The figures are part of a draft and have not yet been enacted.
candidates.title: Ukraine proposes record 2027 defense budget

candidates.summary: Switzerland’s lower house approved the EFTA trade agreement with the Mercosur countries by 118 votes to 66, with 10 abstentions, after adding 517 million Swiss francs in support for farmers over six years. The upper house had already backed the corresponding bill, but the agreement is likely to face a referendum and has not yet taken effect.
candidates.title: Swiss parliament advances Mercosur trade agreement

candidates.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced the abolition of annual road tax for 14.5 million cars and motorcycles. Reuters said the measure was estimated to cost state finances more than €2 billion and came ahead of the following year’s national election. The available report described the policy announcement but did not establish that the tax change had already taken effect.
candidates.title: Meloni announces road-tax abolition for most Italian vehicles

candidates.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee unanimously raised the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage point to 3.75%-4%, saying inflation remained elevated despite solid economic growth. The new target range and related implementation measures take effect September 17.
candidates.title: Federal Reserve raises interest-rate target by quarter point

candidates.summary: The United States removed Venezuela from its list of countries deemed to have demonstrably failed to meet international drug-control commitments, ending a designation applied since 2005. President Donald Trump cited cooperation with Venezuela’s interim government. Venezuela remains classified as a major drug-transit or drug-producing country, and Trump said Colombia could lose its separate failed-demonstrably designation if it makes progress over the coming year.
candidates.title: U.S. removes Venezuela from drug-control failure list

candidates.summary: Swedish public broadcaster SVT projected that the center-left opposition led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson would secure the most seats in the parliamentary election after 99% of votes had been counted. Preliminary figures indicated a 175-174 seat split between the opposition and the governing right-wing bloc. Sweden’s election authority said the final result was not yet complete.
candidates.title: SVT projects Swedish center-left election victory

candidates.summary: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres called for international guardrails to make artificial intelligence safe, transparent and accountable. He said isolated voluntary pauses would not address risks amid geopolitical competition and pointed to the UN-founded Independent International Scientific Panel on AI as a source of evidence for global discussions.
candidates.title: Guterres urges international cooperation on AI safeguards

candidates.summary: A large crowd marched in Valletta demanding accountability for the 2017 car-bomb murder of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Civil-society groups organized the protest two weeks after a jury acquitted businessman Yorgen Fenech of complicity in the murder and criminal association. Malta’s attorney general was expected to appeal on points of law.
candidates.title: Malta protest demands justice for murdered journalist

candidates.summary: India and Pakistan summoned each other’s senior diplomats to lodge protests over Tuesday’s collision between their naval vessels in international waters in the northern Arabian Sea. India said a Pakistani ship approached an Indian warship at high speed in violation of a bilateral separation agreement. No major damage was reported.
candidates.title: India and Pakistan exchange protests over naval collision
